overall_summary: The channel has a very small sample size of low view counts (max 36 views) and almost zero engagement, making statistical confidence low. However, 'self respect' and smartphone-related micro-interactions (like deleted chats or unsaved numbers) show slight relative traction compared to abstract late-night thoughts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on phone behaviors (e.g., 'उंगली उसी चैट पर रुकी थी', 'बिना नाम के सेव किया था नंबर') achieved the highest relative views (36 and 24 views).
winning_patterns.action: Continue anchoring hooks around everyday smartphone UI habits related to ex-partners.

winning_patterns.evidence: Topic 'self respect' generated the channel's top viewed video ('चैट डिलीट करने की हिम्मत', 36 views).
winning_patterns.action: Lean into empowerment and letting go rather than purely helpless sadness.

weak_patterns.evidence: Broad late-night concepts like 'रात के दो बजे' (12 views) or 'मेज पर रखी चाय ठंडी हो गई' (5 views) underperformed.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid overly poetic or cliché weather/tea metaphors; ground stories in tangible modern objects and actions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered entirely around waiting without action (e.g., 'नंबर ब्लॉक नहीं किया कभी') resulted in very low views (5 views).
weak_patterns.action: Ensure every script has a micro-movement toward closure or self-preservation.

next_video.concept: Removing someone from the phone's blocked list because they no longer matter enough to keep restricted.
next_video.opening_direction: ब्लॉक लिस्ट से उसका नंबर अनब्लॉक करने की उंगली उठी,
next_video.twist_direction: लगा था कि शायद दर्द होगा, पर अहसास हुआ कि अब उस नंबर का वजूद ही फोन से मिट चुका है—वो अब अजनबी भी नहीं रहा।
next_video.reason: Previous successful self-respect videos performed best when posted in the early afternoon window around 13:45-13:52.

experiment: Testing if flipping the narrative from 'keeping/deleting a chat' to 'unblocking because of indifference' increases engagement.
